feature1.name: feature_intro
feature1.label: Overview
feature1.title: A Middle Name Generator That Judges the Whole Name
feature1.description: A middle name is never chosen alone. This tool fits it into the complete string — first, middle, last — the way readers and signing tables will meet it.

items.title: Full-name fit, not a list
items.description: Keep the first and last name you already trust. Every direction shows the complete name, so you judge the fit you'll actually print.

items.title: Cadence you can hear
items.description: Each direction comes with a short, hedged note on how the full name sounds spoken — a short middle gives the surname more weight, a long one adds a formal stride.

items.title: A story signal, not decoration
items.description: The middle name should tell the reader something — inherited, rebellious, ceremonial. Every direction explains what it signals in the story or byline.

how_to_use.name: how_to_use
how_to_use.label: HOW TO USE
how_to_use.title: How to Use the Middle Name Generator in 3 Steps
how_to_use.description: Take a half-finished name from first draft to three complete directions in under a minute with this middle name generator.

items.title: Enter what you already have
items.description: Type the first and last name (both optional), pick the setting, era, and the tone the middle name should carry — restrained, inherited, rebellious, and more.

items.title: Compare three directions
items.description: Read each full name aloud with its cadence note and story signal. Check the initials preview, favorite what clicks, and reroll for new directions.

items.title: Continue with the character
items.description: Copy the winning full name, or take it straight into the OC builder, a backstory, or a story prompt and keep writing.

feature2.name: feature_benefits
feature2.label: Benefits
feature2.title: Why the Middle Name Matters in Fiction
feature2.description: The middle name is where rhythm, initials, and family history meet — and where lazy naming shows first.

items.title: Rhythm you can hear
items.description: Three names in a row have a beat. The right middle name controls pacing — clipped and professional, or flowing and ceremonial — before a reader knows why.

items.title: Initials that don't backfire
items.description: Elena V. Hart and Elena S. Hart are different characters on a monogrammed briefcase. The initials preview shows the acronym the full name spells.

items.title: A family layer without exposition
items.description: An inherited middle name implies grandparents, wills, and expectations in a single line of dialogue — backstory you never have to narrate.

items.title: Gender-neutral picks
items.description: Tone-first generation with no gender controls: middles judged only by how they read in the full name.

items.title: Can I use a generated middle name in my fiction?
items.description: Yes. The suggestions are original combinations meant as creative starting points. Names are common cultural material, so a full name you assemble here is yours to use — just avoid modeling a character's full name on a real, identifiable living person.

items.title: How is this different from the Pen Name Generator?
items.description: The Pen Name Generator invents complete bylines from scratch. This tool completes a name you already have — it keeps your first and last name exactly as written and fits a middle name into the full string for a character or a byline.

items.title: How do I avoid an awkward initials problem?
items.description: Type the letters you want to avoid into 'Initials to avoid'. The initials preview shows the acronym each direction spells, and flags any direction whose initials use a letter you excluded.

items.title: Does the tool check whether a name is available?
items.description: No. The middle name generator makes no claims about trademarks, domains, legal names, or uniqueness. If you plan to publish under a name, search it in quotes, check retailer author pages, and search the trademark registries that apply to your market first.

items.title: Can I ask for a name from a specific culture?
items.description: You can describe the sound or family tradition you want in the note field. The tool never claims a name's origin, meaning, or authenticity, and it never presents cultural inference as fact — it fits names by how they read in your setting.

items.title: Should every character have a middle name?
items.description: No — and that's a real choice. A character with no middle name can read as plain-spoken, self-made, or from a tradition that doesn't use them. If the middle name adds nothing, cut it.

items.title: Do you store the names I enter?
items.description: No. First and last names are used only to build your generation request, are never written to logs or analytics, and are not retained after the response returns.
